the-mad-podcast-with-matt-turck.name: The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck
the-mad-podcast-with-matt-turck.bio: Podcast: How to Build Long-Horizon AI Agents — Mitch Troyanovsky, Basis

html_en:
Two quiet but consequential shifts defined today in AI: OpenAI's frontier models are now free for everyone, while the deeper question of how to actually deploy agents for real work — not demos — is finally getting serious, rigorous answers.

The Free Frontier: GPT-5.6 Sol for All

The price of intelligence just hit zero — at least for text. Sam Altman announced today that ChatGPT free users now get unlimited text chat powered by GPT-5.6 Sol, the same model that's been wowing paying subscribers. The reception was immediate.

"You can just ask Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol the wildest things and it will just do it. I talk to it for 5 minutes straight with things that just seem to require weeks of work, get up to get something in the fridge, pet the dog, come back and... it's done." — @thsottiaux

For the broader market, Peter Yang offered a clear-eyed take on where the real battle lies:

"Consumer is basically ChatGPT and Google's market to lose in my opinion... I don't think having access to the best model is that important to normies vs. getting the user onboarding right. My non-AI pilled friends could care less about Sol vs Fable as long as the pricing is fair and the model can get their work done reliably." — @petergyang

Meanwhile, Anthropic made its own quiet capability expansion: Claude Fable 5's biology safeguards were updated, reducing biology-related fallbacks by 85% across product surfaces — a meaningful step toward making frontier models genuinely useful for health and educational questions without the reflexive over-caution that has frustrated researchers.

The Agent Reality Check: It's Closer to Management Than Magic

The most substantive conversation of the day came from Matt Turck's deep-dive podcast with Mitch Troyanovsky, co-founder of Basis — an accounting-focused AI unicorn whose agents run autonomously for hours or days at a time. It's a reference episode for anyone serious about building agents that actually ship.

Watch/Listen: How to Build Long-Horizon AI Agents — Mitch Troyanovsky, Basis (The MAD Podcast)

Troyanovsky's framing of the core challenge is bracingly honest:

"Humans are already used to working with non-deterministic systems, it's just the systems are normally their co-workers, not their computers. And in many ways, companies and processes is all about how do you design a system for non-deterministic entities to coordinate together to solve a problem? And once you realize that, it's like, well, now it's just kind of agent design." — Mitch Troyanovsky, Basis

On the gap between evals and production reality, he was equally direct:

"Let's say you have 100 evals. They all pass. Are you confident that now generalizes to the real world, to production? Our answer has been no. Even if you got it right 100 out of 100 times, if a person is just getting it right because they're going to Wikipedia, the accounting firm wouldn't hire them, and so they shouldn't hire us either." — Mitch Troyanovsky, Basis

Box CEO Aaron Levie echoed this framing in a broader enterprise context:

"Prompting an agent is closer to writing a spec than asking a question. You have to scope the task extensively and define what 'done' looks like... The real upside of agents is when you start to change the underlying workflow itself instead of just treating it as another system you ask questions of." — @levie

No-Code's Quiet Funeral, and the Vindication of "Solve Code Itself"

Airtable's stumbles offered a moment of vindication for Amjad Masad, Replit's founder, who spent years arguing the no-code thesis was fundamentally broken:

"Airtable bookends the rise and fall of 'no code.' I remember arguing endlessly with investors about this. UI can never let you build arbitrary software. The way to make software accessible was always to solve code itself. For a long time, that sounded delusional. Not anymore." — @amasad

Masad also revealed he was pitching code-specific model training to Google, Meta, and others back in 2021-22 — and getting turned down. Replit eventually trained its own. The rest, as they say, is history.

On the infrastructure side, Guillermo Rauch made the case for open, extensible AI coding agents as the defining developer tooling moment of the era:

"Devtools must be open source and universally extensible. AI coding agents are the most important devtools in the history of our industry. Build a Plugin → get exposure to the tidal wave of software creation from every agent: CLIs, IDEs, cloud agents, and even personal assistants." — @rauchg

Claude Meets the Apple Ecosystem

A quietly significant developer story: Anthropic released a Swift package enabling Apple developers to use Claude through Apple's Foundation Models framework — meaning on-device models handle fast, local tasks, and Claude steps in for multi-step reasoning, web search, and code generation. The handoff is seamless to the end user.

The practical pattern is elegant: a journaling app generates daily prompts on-device, then asks Claude to find threads across months of entries. A study app defines a term locally, then hands off to Claude when the student asks why it matters for everything else they've covered. The framework ships with iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27. Apple's install base just became Claude's distribution channel.

One More Thing: How to Think Clearly

A surprisingly resonant workplace observation from @realmadhuguru that doubles as quiet AI workflow advice:

"I've noticed people are much clearer when they speak through new ideas than writing a doc on it. Somewhere between their mouth and the doc, the core idea gets buried as they try to add context, polish it and make it sound smart. So here's what I ask my teams to do: record yourself explaining the idea exactly as you would to a friend, use AI to do basic cleanup but keep the rough original structure and flow. Share that doc." — @realmadhuguru

Troyanovsky's entire team whispers into microphones at their desks for exactly this reason. The pattern is spreading.
html_zh:
今天的AI世界里，两条主线交织而行：模型能力的快速普及正在重塑普通用户的预期，而如何让智能体真正"做成事"，依然是业界最烧脑的工程难题。

🚀 OpenAI与Anthropic同日出招：模型能力全面下放

今天最受关注的产品动态，来自两家头部AI公司几乎同步的战略举动。Sam Altman 宣布，ChatGPT免费用户现可享受无限量文字对话，并搭载升级后的 GPT-5.6 Sol 模型：

"5.6 Sol在对话中表现大幅提升——免费用户现可无限量文字聊天！" —— @sama

用户的反馈相当热烈。@thsottiaux 对 Codex 配合 GPT-5.6 Sol 的体验尤为兴奋：

"你可以对它提出最疯狂的需求，它真的会去做。我跟它聊了五分钟，说了一堆看起来要花好几周才能完成的事，起身去冰箱拿东西、顺手撸了一下狗，回来之后——全做完了。" —— @thsottiaux

与此同时，Anthropic 也在 Claude Fable 5 的生物学安全过滤上进行了大幅松绑，宣布将生物相关的误拦截率降低约85%。官方声明写道：

"我们相信AI最大的正向影响将发生在生物学与医学领域，我们致力于将前沿智能安全地交到尽可能多的研究者手中。" —— @claudeai

此外，Anthropic 还发布了面向Apple开发者的Foundation Models框架支持，通过新的 Swift 软件包，允许开发者在苹果原生框架中无缝调用Claude处理复杂推理任务——用户看到的是一个流畅体验，背后是本地小模型与Claude的分工协作。

🤖 智能体的真正难题：不是技术，是流程设计

在产品发布的热闹之外，今天围绕"如何构建真正可用的长时程智能体"的讨论更值得细读。Matt Turck 与 Basis 联合创始人 Mitch Troyanovsky 的深度对谈（Watch/Listen: How to Build Long-Horizon AI Agents — MAD Podcast）堪称本周最值得收听的一期播客。

Basis 的智能体可以独立运行数小时乃至数天，完整处理报税申报等复杂任务。Mitch 对"通过了100个评测就等于可以上线"的思维定式提出了直接挑战：

"就算你100次全部答对，如果一个人答对是因为他在查维基百科，会计事务所不会雇用他，我们也不应该被雇用。" —— Mitch Troyanovsky

他还分享了一个让不少工程师扎心的观察：

"你会看到有人为一个没有抽象的代码文件抓狂，但他的上下文（context）写得一塌糊涂。英文上下文比代码更珍贵，因为它直接影响模型的表现，代码本身不影响。" —— Mitch Troyanovsky

Aaron Levie 也从企业侧呼应了这一判断：

"提示一个智能体，更像是写一份规格说明书，而不是提一个问题。你必须充分界定任务范围，并定义'完成'是什么样子的……真正的收益，来自于你开始改变底层工作流本身，而不只是把它当成另一个问答系统。" —— @levie

📱 消费级市场：ChatGPT与Google的双雄格局

Peter Yang 对消费级AI市场的竞争格局提出了一个冷静的判断，值得关注：

"消费级市场基本上是ChatGPT和Google的天下，输掉的话只能怪自己。ChatGPT已有10亿用户，需要让他们接入常用应用并用智能体完成工作……最大的障碍是：普通用户不信任AI完全访问他们的数据，以及普通用户根本不知道ChatGPT现在能做什么。在这两点上，营销和信息传递与产品改进同等重要。" —— @petergyang

他的结论颇具洞见：对普通用户来说，模型是Sol还是Fable其实无关紧要，关键是定价合理、用起来靠谱，以及新用户引导流程够不够顺畅。

💻 "无代码"已死，代码本身才是答案

Replit CEO Amjad Masad 今天发了一条颇具历史回顾意味的推文，既是对"无代码运动"的盖棺定论，也是对自己早年判断的一次印证：

"Airtable标志着'无代码'运动的兴衰。UI永远无法让你构建任意软件。让软件变得触手可及的方式，始终是解决代码本身的问题。很长一段时间里，这听起来像是痴人说梦。现在不是了。" —— @amasad

他还披露，早在2021/2022年，他就曾游说谷歌、Meta等公司联合训练代码专属模型，却无人问津——最终Replit自己训练了 Replit-code-3b，才让整个行业"开窍"。

Guillermo Rauch 则为AI编程工具的开放生态站台，强调AI编程智能体的插件标准必须开源且可普遍扩展：

"AI编程智能体是我们这个行业历史上最重要的开发者工具。构建一个插件，就能让你的工作暴露在软件创作浪潮的每一个节点：CLI、IDE、云端智能体，乃至个人助理。" —— @rauchg

💰 融资备忘：给正在融资的创始人的直白建议

最后，投资人 @nikunj 今天发布了一份"VC不会告诉你的融资真相"，在创业者圈子里广泛传播。几条要点特别值得记下：

"不要说谎。硅谷和纽约小得令人发指。如果你说你拿到了某家的Term Sheet，发一条短信就能核实……任何你不想被传播的东西，就不要分享。" —— @nikunj

他还指出，成熟的领投基金很少接受低于10%稀释率的交易，而估值博弈中最忌讳的一招，是拿竞争对手的融资价格来做比较——"你根本不知道那笔交易是怎么谈成的。"
